seed_answers.q1: The manual says 'offer the loyalty credit when the customer threatens to cancel', but it never says the credit only posts if there was no plan change in the last 60 days. The billing system at Globe silently rejects it on day 61 and the customer calls back angrier. So before I promise anything I check the plan-change date, and if they are inside the 60-day window I tell them the exact day it becomes available instead of saying 'I applied it'. The manual also never says that a SIM swap resets that 60-day counter, which I learned after three callbacks in one week.
seed_answers.q2: New hires reset the billing cycle date when a customer asks about proration. It sounds helpful, but the system then bills the old cycle and the new one in the same month, so the customer sees roughly double, for example 2,400 pesos instead of 1,200. The right move is to explain the prorated amount for the remaining days and never touch the cycle date. The second mistake is promising a roaming waiver before pulling the toggle history. If the customer switched roaming on themselves, the waiver gets reversed by audit within 5 days.
seed_answers.q3: I refused a retroactive roaming waiver. The customer, reachable at juan.delacruz@example.com and also maria.santos@example.com for his wife, had turned roaming on himself. His number was +63 917 123 4567 and hers +63 918 765 4321. I offered a 20% goodwill credit instead and documented the toggle history so the next agent would not reopen it.
seed_answers.q4: A customer on a family plan moved abroad mid-cycle while the three dependents stayed in Manila. The script had no branch for the primary line leaving the country. If I cancelled the primary line the dependents would lose the family discount immediately and get billed at single-line rates. I split the plan effective at the next cycle date, kept the dependents on the family discount, and manually adjusted 14 days of prorated charges, which came to 42.10 dollars. I also set a reminder to confirm the split actually posted, because Siebel sometimes drops the dependents' discount on the first bill.

followup_answers.f1: At day 58 or 59 I escalate to the retention desk instead of refusing, because the system backdates the plan change on day 61 and a plain refusal gets reversed anyway. My threshold is 3 days before the 60-day mark. If the customer is at day 30, I give the exact date and offer a one-time 100 peso courtesy credit so they do not call back angry.
followup_answers.f2: For the family plan split I used the remaining days in the cycle, 14 out of 30, times the primary line's daily rate, 3.01 dollars, which gave 42.10 dollars. I only do a manual split if the dependents are at least two lines, because for one dependent the family discount is smaller than the proration headache and I just move them to a single plan.
followup_answers.f3: The exception to my 60-day rule is a customer who changed plans because of our own outage credit. Those changes are flagged as system-initiated, and the loyalty credit posts anyway. I check the change reason code before refusing, roughly one in ten cases is this.
